_about: Every tunable number for the signal pack. Edit a value, then run `python3 scripts/apply_weights.py`: it recomputes every weighted number in signals/pack/ from the raw inputs each signal keeps, so you never need the original feed. All values are starting priors; change them to test your own view.

link_confidence._about: How sure a signal reaches ANT, or a named company, through each link (impact rows, link_confidence).

source_reliability._about: Starting trust in a source. Patterns are matched against the source name and outlet, first match wins.
patterns: financial times|ft\.com|wall street journal|wsj|new york times|nytimes|cnbc|guardian|techcrunch|the verge|mit technology review|the information|axios|fortune|business insider|forbes|wired|ars technica|semafor|economist

half_life_days._about: How long a signal counts. A signal takes the longest half-life among its categories; horizon_days is twice it.

grade_scale._about: A classifier's word grades as numbers.

strength_full_at._about: The size at which strength reaches 1.0; smaller sizes scale linearly.

build._about: Used only when the organisers build the pack from AlphaStreet's feed (organisers/). Changing these has no effect on apply_weights.py.

dedup._about: How near-duplicate headlines are merged and stories clustered.

relevance._about: Which graded feed signals are kept when pulling. Linked companies are in signals/companies.csv.
